title: Синтетические респонденты в анкетном опросе: эмпирическая проверка на данных опроса студентов / Synthetic Respondents in Survey Research: An Empirical Test Against a Student Survey
description:
Preprint (Russian original + author's English version). Не проходил рецензирование / Not peer reviewed.

The paper tests empirically the limits of applicability of synthetic respondents — large language models answering survey questions on behalf of "digital twins" built from the socio-demographic characteristics of real people. The benchmark is the author's own survey of RANEPA students ("Scientific Code" programme, 2024, N = 1,795, 39 items), in which every human answer is known. Each twin was built from five attributes taken as a whole from one respondent's row; DeepSeek re-answered 36 coded questions in 64,620 independent calls.

The twin reproduces the central tendency and the direction of demographic differences (gender differences matched on 85% of items) but systematically narrows the spread of answers (mean SD 0.52 vs. 1.04), avoids extreme scale points (36% vs. 50%) and the "hard to say" option, weakens associations between answers from different thematic blocks threefold (mean |r| 0.10 vs. 0.27) and does not convey individuality (own twin 37.9% vs. random twin 36.5%). Three levels of synthetic-respondent behaviour are distinguished (distributions, spread, associations and individual answers). Conclusion: a synthetic respondent is a means of preparing measurement (questionnaire pretesting), not a measurement instrument. A hypothesis is formulated on using human–twin discrepancies to detect socially desirable responding.
